PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-08-05
60F, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. She reports feeling generally well, with good energy and regular morning walks. She takes her blood pressure medication daily and checks readings at home. Over the past few weeks she noticed mild ankle swelling by evening that resolves overnight, prompting a cardiac screen today. No shortness of breath. She works as a school administrator. Mother with breast cancer. Appetite is good; diet includes some sugary snacks, which were discussed. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 164 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace ankle edema, improves with elevation.
Labs (this week): A1c 6.0%, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR stable post-transplant, BNP 42 pg/mL.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue current antihypertensive. Home readings reviewed, averaging 124/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. History of chronic kidney disease stage 4, resolved after kidney transplant. Graft function stable; continue immunosuppression as directed by the transplant team. Labs reviewed and acceptable.
3. R/o CHF; BNP normal. Ankle swelling is mild, improves overnight, and fits long hours seated at her desk; no echocardiogram needed. Advised leg elevation in the evenings and short walking breaks at work.
4. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary snacks and continuing daily walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
5. Family history: discussed mother's history and confirmed mammography is up to date.
6. Health maintenance: colorectal screening up to date; influenza vaccine offered this fall.

Return in 3 months for routine follow-up, sooner for worsening swelling.
